hero.body:
House Passes Major Defense Bill With $900 Billion in Funding

The House of Representatives voted 312-112 to approve a sweeping defense policy bill that authorizes $900 billion in military spending and includes provisions for troop pay raises and weapons purchases reform.

The 3,000-page National Defense Authorization Act represents the annual legislation that typically receives bipartisan support. The White House has indicated support for the measure, which aligns with the administration's national security priorities.

The bill includes a 3.8% pay raise for many military members and funds for housing and facility improvements at military bases. It also authorizes $400 million annually for the next two years to manufacture weapons for Ukraine, reflecting lawmakers' commitment to supporting the country against Russian invasion.

The legislation strikes compromises between political parties. It cuts climate-related spending by $1.6 billion and reduces diversity, equity and inclusion funding by $40 million, aligning with Republican priorities. At the same time, it strengthens congressional oversight of the Pentagon and repeals several outdated war authorizations, including the 2003 authorization used to justify the 2003 Iraq invasion.

A significant portion of the bill addresses military accountability. The legislation includes provisions that cut Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth's travel budget by a quarter until the Pentagon provides Congress with unedited video footage of strikes against suspected drug smuggling boats near Venezuela. A September operation killed survivors who were clinging to a partially destroyed vessel. The bill also requires Hegseth to allow Congress to review the orders authorizing these strikes.

The defense bill includes requirements to maintain minimum troop levels in key regions. It mandates keeping at least 76,000 troops and major equipment stationed in Europe unless NATO allies are consulted about withdrawal. Additionally, it sets a minimum requirement of 28,500 US troops in South Korea.

The legislation addresses concerns about military airspace operations over Washington. Several senators from both parties criticized provisions they viewed as insufficient to restrict military flights following a midair collision between an army helicopter and a jetliner that killed all 67 people aboard in September.

Congress uses the bill to repeal sanctions on Syria that were imposed in 2019 under the previous administration. The new Syrian government, led by Ahmed al-Sharaa, is seeking to rebuild the country's economy, and supporters argue that permanent sanction removal will encourage international investment.

Democrats expressed criticism about the removal of a provision that would have expanded in vitro fertilization coverage for active duty personnel. The earlier version of the bill included this medical procedure coverage.

The bill now moves to the Senate, where leaders are working to pass the legislation before Congress departs for the holiday break.

cards.headline: Israel Strikes Hezbollah Targets After New Lebanon Cease-Fire
cards.teaser: Israel said it targeted Hezbollah positions hours after a U.S.-brokered cease-fire with Lebanon was announced.
cards.body:
Israel and Lebanon have agreed to implement a ceasefire brokered by the Trump administration. The agreement requires Hezbollah to cease all fire and withdraw its fighters south of the Litani River in southern Lebanon. The U.S., Lebanon, and Israel issued a joint statement rejecting "any attempt, by any state or non-state actor, to hold Lebanon's future hostage."

However, Israel conducted multiple drone strikes in southern Lebanon following the ceasefire announcement. Hezbollah, which was excluded from the U.S.-led negotiations, said it fired rockets at Israeli targets hours after the truce was announced, raising questions about whether the agreement will hold.

cards.headline: SpaceX targets largest stock market debut in history with $135 per share IPO
cards.body:
SpaceX announced it will sell 555.6 million shares at $135 each in what would become the largest initial public offering in history, seeking to raise approximately $75 billion. The offering is scheduled to commence next week following a roadshow that began this week, in which investment banks pitch the company to potential investors.

At this valuation, SpaceX would achieve a market value of $1.77 trillion, making it worth more than all but five companies in the S&P 500 index. Nvidia, the semiconductor leader, remains the most valuable company at $5.2 trillion.

The IPO could substantially increase founder Elon Musk's wealth. According to Forbes, Musk's current net worth stands at $825 billion, with his SpaceX stake valued at $542 billion. If the offering proceeds as planned, he could become the world's first trillionaire, though he is not selling any personal shares in this offering. Musk will retain 82.4 percent voting power in the company following the IPO.

The space exploration company, formally known as Space Exploration Technologies Corp, was founded in 2002 and has become central to Musk's vision of establishing a self-sufficient city on Mars. SpaceX dominates commercial space transportation and provides crucial services to NASA for most of its rocket launches. The company also operates a satellite internet system and has entered the artificial intelligence sector.

SpaceX acquired Musk's xAI company to develop solar-powered infrastructure supporting AI technology demands. This move aligns with broader industry trends, as competitors including Anthropic and OpenAI are also pursuing public offerings or major fundraising rounds. Alphabet announced this week plans to raise $80 billion in equity specifically to fund artificial intelligence infrastructure investments.

The wave of substantial capital raises across the tech sector reflects efforts to finance the massive datacentres required for AI operations. These fundraising activities underscore how central infrastructure investment has become to competition in advanced technology.

The IPO represents a significant opportunity for the banking sector. Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley are leading the offering, with JP Morgan, Bank of America, Citigroup and 19 other banks participating. Jamie Dimon, CEO of JP Morgan Chase, is hosting a discussion with high-net-worth clients this week to discuss the SpaceX opportunity, according to reports. The discussion will include SpaceX president Gwynne Shotwell and chief financial officer Bret Johnsen.

Market observers expect SpaceX to carry substantial weight in the S&P 500 given its size, meaning most investors with retirement accounts or pension plans will gain exposure to the company's stock performance. The listing comes as markets show mixed signals for technology stocks, though investor enthusiasm for space industry companies appears robust.

cards.headline: Senate begins debate on reconciliation package to fund immigration enforcement
cards.teaser: The Senate started debate Thursday on a budget reconciliation package that would fund immigration enforcement agencies through the end of President Trump's term.
cards.body:
The Senate launched debate Thursday on a budget reconciliation package to fund immigration enforcement agencies through the end of Trump's term. After a party-line procedural vote Wednesday, lawmakers prepared for hours of debate followed by a vote-a-rama—a series of rapid-fire amendment votes.

The reconciliation process allows passage with a simple majority, letting Republicans advance the immigration enforcement funding without Democratic support. The vote-a-rama permits senators to propose unlimited amendments voted on in succession, sometimes stretching for hours. Final passage is expected later this week, after which the legislation must be reconciled with any House version before reaching the president.

cards.headline: Senate Republicans advance ICE funding bill through end of Trump term
cards.teaser: Senate Republicans are moving forward with legislation to fund immigration enforcement agencies through the remainder of the current presidential term.
cards.body:
The Senate is set to begin debate on a bill that would provide funding for Immigration and Customs Enforcement through the end of Trump's presidency. Republican leadership is pushing the measure forward as part of broader immigration enforcement priorities.

The funding legislation comes as immigration policy remains a central focus of the administration. The bill would ensure continuous funding for ICE operations without requiring repeated appropriations battles during the remainder of the term.

cards.headline: Nvidia and Microsoft launch AI-powered Windows PCs with local processing
cards.body:
Nvidia has unveiled a new superchip designed to bring artificial intelligence capabilities directly to personal computers, marking a significant expansion beyond its dominant data center business. The RTX Spark chip, developed in collaboration with Microsoft over three years, will power laptops and desktop computers from major manufacturers including Dell, Lenovo, Asus and HP.

The chip combines a microprocessor and graphics processor, created with assistance from Taiwan's MediaTek. It enables AI agents to run locally on devices rather than relying on cloud computing, allowing the software to navigate computers autonomously and potentially replace traditional mouse and keyboard interactions. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang announced the development at the Computex conference in Taiwan, describing it as a reinvention of the PC for the AI era.

"The chip would reimagine the PC for the first time in 40 years," Huang said, positioning the technology as a fundamental shift in how people interact with computers. Despite the computational power required, Nvidia states that devices using the RTX Spark will remain thin and light.

The move represents Nvidia's push beyond graphics cards into integrated chips that control entire computer systems. The company is also developing the Vera CPU, designed for AI agents and targeted at early adopters including OpenAI, Anthropic and SpaceX.

Industry analysts view the development as transformative. Neil Shah, co-founder of Counterpoint Research, compared the RTX Spark to major technological breakthroughs including the iPhone and ChatGPT. "The RTX Spark looks to transform the traditional app-centric PC to a real useful agentic AI personal computer which will eventually be in every home in coming years," Shah said.

However, analysts caution that while strategically important, this venture into consumer PCs represents a longer-term growth opportunity rather than an immediate earnings driver. Nvidia's current financial performance remains heavily dependent on demand for data center AI infrastructure.

The announcement intensifies competition in the AI chip market. Intel plans to launch its own AI chip later this year, featuring the Xe3P graphics processor codenamed Crescent Island, which the company describes as purpose-built for the emerging generation of AI agents. Apple and Qualcomm also compete in this space.

During his keynote, Huang addressed concerns that artificial intelligence will eliminate jobs. He called suggestions that AI would reduce demand for software engineers "complete nonsense," arguing instead that the technology increases productivity and hiring. "The number of engineers, software engineers, is actually increasing," he stated.

The RTX Spark chips are expected to launch this year, with complete systems anticipated to command premium prices in the laptop market due to the significant hardware resources required for local AI processing.

cards.headline: Trump administration advances AI-powered medical diagnostics program
cards.teaser: A Trump-backed initiative aims to introduce AI doctor systems into American medicine, drawing concern from healthcare providers.
cards.body:
The Trump administration is backing an effort to bring artificial intelligence diagnostic systems into American medical practice. The initiative has generated debate among healthcare professionals, with doctors and providers raising concerns about the technology's implementation and potential effects on medical training.

AI adoption in healthcare has increased, but medical providers have expressed worries about deskilling, where reliance on automated systems could diminish clinical judgment and diagnostic abilities. Some doctors have called AI use in healthcare a concerning development. Proponents argue that AI systems can augment medical decision-making and improve efficiency in healthcare delivery, while critics point to risks in delegating diagnostic responsibilities to automated systems.

hero.headline: Gun Battles Erupt in Somali Capital as Election Dispute Escalates
hero.body:
Fierce clashes between government troops and opposition-aligned militias erupted in Mogadishu on Wednesday afternoon, marking a dramatic escalation of Somalia's political crisis. Residents described the violence as the worst fighting the capital has experienced in years, with heavy gunfire forcing civilians to flee their neighborhoods.

The conflict stems from the president's decision to extend his term beyond its expiration date rather than hold scheduled elections. Opposition leaders, who had embedded themselves with armed militias in their clan strongholds across the city, mobilized their forces in response. The extension of the presidential term without broad political consensus triggered fierce resistance from rival factions and sparked calls for protests.

Somalia's political system has long remained fragile, with a history of delayed and disputed elections compounding tensions between the federal government and regional leaders. The current standoff reflects deeper divisions over governance and power-sharing arrangements that have repeatedly undermined efforts to establish stable democratic institutions in the East African nation.

Residents reported widespread fear as gunfire echoed through neighborhoods, with many taking shelter indoors as clashes intensified across multiple areas. The scale of the violence marked a significant turning point in what had been a building political crisis, raising concerns about the country's trajectory moving forward.

The fighting threatens to undermine Somalia's recent security progress. In recent years, the country has made gradual advances against the militant group al-Shabab, but political infighting among Somalia's own leaders risks destabilizing these gains. When political leaders cannot resolve disputes peacefully, security institutions become vulnerable and extremist groups can exploit the chaos.

The international community has repeatedly urged Somali political leaders to resolve their differences through dialogue and to hold elections without unreasonable delay. Analysts and observers warn that the extension of the presidential term without consensus threatens to deepen the crisis further and potentially trigger sustained violence in the capital.

The violence began in the runup to opposition-organized protests scheduled for Thursday, suggesting that tensions had been building for weeks. Opposition leaders viewed the term extension as a power grab that circumvented democratic processes, while government officials may have argued that electoral preparations required more time.

How quickly Somalia's political leaders can negotiate a path forward will likely determine whether these clashes represent an isolated outbreak of violence or the beginning of prolonged conflict in Mogadishu. The window for resolving the dispute through dialogue appears to be narrowing as armed groups take active roles in the political standoff. Without immediate diplomatic intervention, the risk of further escalation remains significant, potentially destabilizing the broader region and undermining international efforts to strengthen Somalia's fragile state institutions.

cards.headline: Hezbollah Fiber-Optic Drones Breach Israeli Defenses
cards.teaser: Drone attacks by the Lebanese militant group have caught Israeli forces off guard, prompting officials to search for countermeasures.
cards.body:
Hezbollah has deployed drones equipped with fiber-optic technology in attacks that have exposed vulnerabilities in Israeli air defenses. The strikes caught Israeli political and military leadership off guard, prompting urgent efforts to develop countermeasures. IDF northern chief Rafi Milo narrowly escaped one drone strike.

The fiber-optic technology has proven difficult for Israel's existing defense systems to detect and intercept, presenting a significant new aerial threat that Israeli officials are now working to address.

cards.headline: Marjane Satrapi, Persepolis Author, Dies at 56
cards.teaser: The graphic novelist whose memoir depicted life during the Islamic Revolution and Iran-Iraq War has died.
cards.body:
Marjane Satrapi, the French-Iranian author and illustrator best known for her graphic novel series Persepolis, has died at age 56. Her acclaimed memoir, published in the early 2000s, offered readers an intimate account of growing up during Iran's Islamic Revolution and the Iran-Iraq War through stark black-and-white illustrations and compelling storytelling.

Persepolis became a landmark work that reshaped international perceptions of Iran and was adapted into an Oscar-nominated animated film. The graphic novel became a staple in literature curricula worldwide, introducing generations of readers to the personal human costs of political upheaval. According to her family, Satrapi died of sadness following the death of her husband, Swedish producer Mattias Ripa, last year.

cards.headline: Four Killed in Ukrainian Attacks on Occupied Crimea
cards.teaser: Russian-backed officials accused Ukraine of launching attacks that killed four people and injured at least 10 others.
cards.body:
The provided sources are about different stories:
BBC News covers Iranian drone strikes on Kuwait airport
The Guardian reports on rebel attacks in eastern DRC related to Ebola response

Neither source pertains to the Ukrainian attacks on occupied Crimea. Therefore, I'm returning the original card text unchanged:

At least four people were killed and 10 injured in attacks on occupied Crimea that Russian-backed officials attributed to Ukraine. The strikes targeted areas under Russian control since the 2014 annexation of the peninsula.

The attacks represent the latest violence in the ongoing conflict between Russia and Ukraine, with Crimea serving as a frequent flashpoint. Ukraine has previously struck Russian military targets and infrastructure on the peninsula, viewing such operations as legitimate efforts to reclaim occupied territory.

cards.headline: Police Warn Tiananmen Families Not to Visit Graves on Anniversary
cards.teaser: Authorities told relatives of those killed in the 1989 crackdown to stay away from cemeteries on the 37th anniversary.
cards.body:
Chinese police warned families of people killed in the 1989 Tiananmen Square crackdown not to visit graves on the 37th anniversary of the event. The directive reflected escalating restrictions on public remembrance of the violent suppression of pro-democracy protests.

The United States and China clashed over the anniversary, with the U.S. Consulate in Hong Kong issuing a statement marking the occasion. Taiwan called on China to face the historical facts of what happened. Amnesty International described the cemetery ban as heartless and a signal of intensifying repression against those who seek to preserve the memory of the crackdown.

cards.headline: Trump Endorses Dual U.S.-Colombia Citizen in Colombian Runoff
cards.teaser: President Trump backed right-wing candidate Abelardo De La Espriella, who holds citizenship in both countries.
cards.body:
President Trump endorsed Abelardo De La Espriella, a dual U.S.-Colombian citizen, in Colombia's presidential runoff election. De La Espriella is running as a right-wing candidate in the closely watched race.

The endorsement raises constitutional questions about whether a U.S. citizen can serve as Colombia's president under the country's requirements. Trump's public backing of a candidate in another nation's election represents an unusual intervention in South American politics.

Israel and Lebanon have agreed to implement a ceasefire contingent on Hezbollah halting its attacks. The United States stated that both countries reject "any attempt, by any state or non-state actor, to hold Lebanon's future hostage."

The agreement represents a significant diplomatic development in efforts to reduce conflict in the Middle East.

cards.headline: Marjane Satrapi, author of Persepolis, dies at 56
cards.teaser: The French-Iranian author and illustrator known for her graphic novel series and Oscar-nominated film has died.
cards.body:

cards.headline: Israeli strikes kill 11 in Gaza City, medics report
cards.teaser: Women and children were among those killed when Israeli aircraft struck residential buildings in multiple areas of Gaza City.
cards.body:
Israeli aircraft struck at least four residential buildings across several neighborhoods in Gaza City, killing at least 11 people according to medical officials. Women and children were among those killed in the strikes.

The attacks targeted multiple residential areas simultaneously across different parts of the city.

cards.headline: Justice Department considers alternative payouts after settlement fund faces pushback
cards.teaser: The Justice Department is exploring other options for compensating individuals after its proposed $1.8 billion settlement fund encountered opposition.
cards.body:
Officials at the Justice Department are examining alternative methods to provide payments following resistance to a planned $1.8 billion settlement fund. Trump told reporters he does not know whether the original fund proposal is dead.

The fund was intended to compensate defendants in cases the administration described as weaponization of the justice system. After facing pushback, the department is now considering other approaches to fulfill what Trump called reimbursement obligations for those affected.

cards.headline: Bondi Beach shooting hero charged with domestic assault
cards.teaser: Ahmed al Ahmed, who disarmed one of the shooters during a deadly attack at a Jewish event, now faces domestic assault charges.
cards.body:
Ahmed al-Ahmed, the 44-year-old Sydney man who disarmed one of the gunmen during December's Bondi Beach attack, has been charged with assaulting his father. Police allege he put his father in a headlock on 9 March at a house in Bankstown, in Sydney's west.

The domestic assault charges are separate from the shooting incident where al-Ahmed was hailed as a hero for his intervention.

cards.headline: Stock futures fall as Broadcom leads semiconductor decline

Stock index futures fell as semiconductor stocks declined, with Broadcom leading the drop after releasing its earnings results. The Dow futures showed gains while Nasdaq futures sank, reflecting divergent performance across sectors.

Broadcom's results prompted a broader pullback in chip stocks, weighing on technology-heavy indexes. The stock market had recently reached record highs, with the S&P 500 posting a record-breaking rally before the momentum slowed. Oil prices eased from recent highs as markets digested the mixed corporate results and adjusted positions.

cards.headline: Quantinuum prices IPO at $60 per share, raises $1.68 billion
cards.teaser: Quantum computing company Quantinuum priced its upsized initial public offering at $60 per share ahead of its Nasdaq debut.
cards.body:
Quantinuum, backed by Honeywell, priced its initial public offering at $60 per share and raised $1.68 billion in an upsized offering. The quantum computing company is set to begin trading on the Nasdaq, marking another public market entry for the emerging quantum computing sector.

The IPO comes as quantum computing gains momentum among investors interested in next-generation computing technology. Quantinuum's debut follows growing attention to quantum computing applications across industries. The company expanded the size of its offering from initial plans, indicating strong investor demand for quantum computing exposure.

cards.headline: Bill Ackman's Pershing Square exits Universal Music stake for $600 million profit
cards.teaser: Pershing Square is set to make $600 million from its Universal Music Group stake after the music company rejected Ackman's takeover proposal.
cards.body:
Bill Ackman's Pershing Square has sold its stake in Universal Music Group, realizing approximately $600 million in profit. The sale follows Universal Music's rejection of Ackman's $64 billion acquisition proposal.

Universal Music shares declined 7 percent following the share offload. The music company opted to remain independent rather than accept Ackman's takeover bid, ending his attempt to gain control of the entertainment firm.

A CEO has informed employees that scheduled salary raises for 2026 are being canceled, with the compensation budget redirected toward artificial intelligence initiatives instead. All eligible employees are affected by this decision.

The move reflects a widespread corporate shift toward AI investment. Companies across industries are channeling substantial resources into AI technology and infrastructure as they pursue competitive advantages through automation and AI-powered systems.

cards.headline: Google releases Gemma 4 model designed to run on laptops with 16GB RAM
cards.teaser: Google DeepMind introduced a multimodal AI model that can operate on standard consumer laptops.

Google launched Gemma 4 12B, a multimodal artificial intelligence model that can run locally on laptops equipped with just 16 gigabytes of RAM. The company also released Google AI Edge Gallery for macOS, allowing Mac users to run Gemini models directly on their computers without cloud connectivity.

The Gemma 4 12B is described as a unified, encoder-free model capable of processing multiple types of data. Google positioned the release as enabling local, agentic workflows where AI operations occur on user devices rather than remote servers. The company published the model through its AI Edge platform, designed to bring Google's AI capabilities to consumer hardware.

cards.headline: Nintendo confirms Switch 2 with replaceable battery for European Union market
cards.teaser: Nintendo will sell a version of its upcoming console with user-replaceable batteries to comply with EU regulations.
cards.body:
Nintendo will launch Switch 2 consoles with user-replaceable batteries in the European Union to comply with new regulations taking effect February 18, 2027. The company has registered the modified hardware designs with EU authorities.

Nintendo stated on its website that it is "implementing measures to comply with these requirements," addressing the EU's mandate for consumer electronics to feature removable batteries.

cards.headline: Waymo repurposes used robotaxi batteries for power grid storage
cards.teaser: Batteries from Waymo's autonomous vehicles will be redeployed in energy storage projects in California and Texas.
cards.body:
Waymo announced it will redirect used batteries from its robotaxi fleet to bolster energy storage infrastructure for electrical grids. The batteries will support storage projects in California and Texas, two states with growing renewable energy capacity and grid stability needs.

The initiative addresses both electronic waste concerns and grid-scale energy storage demand. Batteries used in electric vehicles typically retain significant capacity even after their automotive service life ends, making them suitable for stationary storage applications where weight and space constraints are less demanding than in vehicles.

cards.headline: Google shares Fitbit Air blueprints for custom accessory manufacturing
cards.teaser: Google released CAD drawings and specifications allowing anyone to design and produce bands and accessories for the Fitbit Air.
cards.body:
Google published complete CAD drawings and technical specifications for the Fitbit Air, enabling third-party manufacturers and individuals to create custom bands and accessories. The release includes detailed measurements and design guidelines for producing compatible products, including support for bicep band configurations.

The move represents an unusual level of openness for a consumer electronics manufacturer, which typically restricts accessory production to licensed partners. Google has not explained whether the blueprint release is intended to encourage a broader accessory ecosystem or address specific user requests for unconventional mounting options like arm bands.

cards.headline: Oura releases Ring 5, 40% smaller than previous model
cards.teaser: The health tracking company launched what it describes as the world's smallest smart ring, priced starting at $399.
cards.body:
Oura has unveiled the Ring 5, positioning it as the world's smallest smart ring. The new device is 40 percent smaller than its predecessor and maintains the company's health monitoring capabilities in a more compact design. Pricing begins at $399.

The Ring 5 features a thinner, lighter construction. The Verge is conducting a full review to assess the device's durability and battery life claims, along with new software updates that have begun rolling out.

cards.headline: Benchmark raises $2 billion, launches first growth-stage fund
cards.teaser: The venture capital firm abandoned its tradition of limiting funds to $425 million and created a growth-stage vehicle.
cards.body:
Benchmark announced a $2 billion capital raise that includes the firm's first growth-stage fund, ending a practice of more than 20 years of keeping individual funds at approximately $425 million. The expansion marks a strategic shift for the venture capital firm, which has historically focused on early-stage investments.

The decision to raise larger funds and enter growth-stage investing reflects broader trends in venture capital, where firms increasingly seek to support portfolio companies through later funding rounds. Benchmark has not disclosed the specific allocation between its traditional early-stage fund and the new growth vehicle.

hero.headline: Knicks defeat Spurs in Game 1 of NBA Finals
hero.body:
The New York Knicks won Game 1 of the NBA Finals against the San Antonio Spurs with a 105-95 victory in San Antonio on Wednesday night. The win extended the Knicks' remarkable playoff streak to 11 consecutive victories and moved them three wins away from their first championship since 1973.

The Knicks entered the game as heavy favorites despite facing Victor Wembanyama, described as the most exciting player in the world. The Spurs had earned their Finals berth by defeating the defending champion Oklahoma City Thunder in the previous round. However, the Knicks kept Wembanyama quiet for long stretches throughout the contest.

The game was tightly contested, with the Spurs leading by 14 points in the third quarter. The Knicks, demonstrating the same resilience that defined their playoff run, mounted a comeback similar to their Game 1 victory against the Cavaliers in the Eastern Conference Finals, when they overcame a 22-point deficit. New York took a 78-76 lead early in the fourth quarter before putting together an 11-0 run to close out the game.

Jalen Brunson was instrumental in the victory, particularly down the stretch. He finished with 30 points, including 13 in the fourth quarter. "Just sticking together, it wasn't really our night and wasn't really my night most of the night but we kept finding a way, kept chipping away," Brunson said after the game. "Just knowing we have each other's back, there's a lot of things we could have done better, but I think our togetherness was really the biggest difference."

OG Anunoby also stepped up when it mattered, scoring 12 of his 17 points in the fourth quarter. The Knicks demonstrated excellent execution down the stretch, recording no turnovers in the final quarter.

Wembanyama led the Spurs with 26 points, 12 rebounds, and three blocks, but he was far from his dominant best. He shot just 6-for-21 from the field and acknowledged his poor performance. "I was bad tonight, it's not more complicated than that," Wembanyama said. He denied that nerves or the occasion affected the team's performance.

The Spurs struggled in the fourth quarter, committing five turnovers while shooting just 28.6 percent from the field.

Brunson had an injury scare of his own, colliding with Harrison Barnes at the end of the first quarter. He briefly left the game with a knee injury but returned in the second quarter and appeared to aggravate an ankle injury but remained in the game.

Game 2 takes place Friday night in San Antonio before the series shifts to Madison Square Garden on Monday for what is expected to be a raucous Game 3.

cards.headline: Patriots acquire wide receiver A.J. Brown from Eagles in trade
cards.teaser: The New England Patriots completed a trade to acquire wide receiver A.J. Brown from the Philadelphia Eagles after pursuing him for two years.
cards.body:
The Patriots acquired wide receiver A.J. Brown from the Eagles in a trade that ended two years of negotiations. Philadelphia had previously rejected New England's inquiries about the receiver. Eagles left tackle Jordan Mailata expressed relief after the trade was finalized.

Reactions at Eagles organized team activities were mixed following Brown's departure. The Patriots had been pursuing Brown for an extended period before Philadelphia agreed to the deal. Questions have emerged about whether New England overpaid to acquire the receiver.

cards.headline: Former Ireland rugby player Fergus Slattery dies at 77
cards.teaser: Fergus Slattery, who played back row for Ireland and the British and Irish Lions, has died at the age of 77.
cards.body:
Blackrock College has announced the death of Fergus Slattery, the former Ireland and British and Irish Lions back row forward, at the age of 77.

Slattery enjoyed a distinguished rugby career representing Ireland at international level and was selected for the British and Irish Lions tours, playing as a back row forward during his playing days.

cards.headline: FIFA bans reusable water bottles from World Cup stadiums
cards.teaser: FIFA announced fans cannot bring reusable water bottles into World Cup stadiums, citing safety concerns in a late policy change that heat experts have criticized.
cards.body:
FIFA has updated its World Cup stadium code of conduct to ban reusable water bottles, reversing an earlier policy that allowed empty, transparent plastic bottles inside venues. The organization says the prohibition is necessary to prevent risk and injury to players and attendees. The ban also extends to other containers including bottles, cups, jars, and cans that could be thrown as projectiles.

The last-minute policy change has raised concerns among fans about access to drinking water during the tournament, particularly given the expected heat conditions at World Cup venues.

cards.headline: Manchester City chairman says Guardiola considered quitting multiple times
cards.teaser: Manchester City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak said manager Pep Guardiola had seriously considered quitting on previous occasions before ultimately staying.
cards.body:
Manchester City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak has revealed that manager Pep Guardiola threatened to quit "100 times" during his tenure at the club. Al Mubarak compared Guardiola's repeated threats to The Boy Who Cried Wolf, suggesting many were not serious. The chairman described himself as Guardiola's "psychiatrist" and played a key role in convincing him to stay on multiple occasions.

Guardiola initially joined City on a three-year contract and agreed to four extensions in 2018, 2020, 2022, and 2024, though he was hesitant about each renewal. After 10 years at the club, Guardiola recently departed City, having won 17 major honours during his time in charge.

cards.headline: Manchester City may pursue legal action over Haaland transfer claim
cards.teaser: Manchester City is considering legal action after a Real Madrid presidential candidate displayed an Erling Haaland shirt on live television.
cards.body:
Manchester City is considering legal action against Enrique Riquelme, a candidate in Real Madrid's presidential election, after he displayed a Madrid shirt with Erling Haaland's name during a television appearance. Riquelme claimed a clause in Haaland's contract would allow him to sign the striker if elected president.

On Wednesday, Riquelme stated that Haaland wanted to join Real Madrid and promised that Rodri would also leave City for the Spanish club. Haaland signed a nine-and-a-half-year contract with Manchester City in January 2025.

cards.headline: Browns linebacker Jared Verse says he can play freely with Carson Schwesinger
cards.teaser: Jared Verse said he can play with more freedom knowing Carson Schwesinger is positioned behind him on the Cleveland Browns defense.
cards.body:
Browns linebacker Jared Verse stated he can play with greater freedom because Carson Schwesinger is behind him. Verse joined Cleveland after being traded from the Los Angeles Rams in a deal that sent Myles Garrett to Los Angeles.

Verse said he is not trying to replace Garrett following the trade. He made his first appearance on the Browns practice field after the transaction.

hero.headline: Marjane Satrapi, Persepolis Author and Director, Dies at 56
hero.body:
Marjane Satrapi, the French-Iranian artist, filmmaker, and graphic novelist whose acclaimed memoir Persepolis reshaped international perceptions of Iran, has died at 56. According to a statement from her relatives provided to French news agency AFP, Satrapi died of sadness following the death of her husband, Swedish producer Mattias Ripa, who passed away on April 8 last year.

Born in 1969 in Rasht, Iran, Satrapi was raised in Tehran by her father, an engineer, and her mother, a dress designer. As a teenager, her parents sent her to Europe to continue her education and escape the restrictions of the Islamic Republic. She eventually settled in France, arriving in 1994 and becoming a French citizen in 2006.

In 2000, Satrapi published Persepolis, a comic book memoir that became an international phenomenon. The work told the story of a rebellious young girl navigating Iran after the 1979 revolution and the establishment of the Islamic Republic, before being sent alone to Europe at age 14. The memoir sold millions of copies and established Satrapi as one of the most widely read Iranian authors in the world. She later described having little expectation the book would be published, telling El País in 2020: "With Persepolis, I didn't even think I'd find a publisher. I thought I'd make 50 photocopies for my friends to read."

Satrapi co-directed the animated film adaptation of Persepolis, which became an international success and earned her a historic place in Oscar history as the first woman nominated for the Academy Award for Best Animated Feature. The film won the Jury Prize at the Cannes Film Festival.

Throughout her career, Satrapi was a vocal opponent of Iran's clerical establishment. She told The Guardian in 2024 that Persepolis aimed to help western readers recognize the humanity of Iranian people, saying they are "actually human beings like us." She stated her work's purpose was to reassure young Iranians that they were heard and supported by the outside world.

Satrapi went on to direct five feature films, including Radioactive (2019), a biographical drama starring Rosamund Pike as scientist Marie Curie. In 2024, she returned to comics by coordinating Woman, Life, Freedom, a collaborative graphic work bringing together 17 Iranian and international comic artists. The book examined the protest movement following the 2022 death in custody of Mahsa Amini, a 22-year-old Kurdish-Iranian woman.

President Emmanuel Macron paid tribute to Satrapi, describing her as "a great artist who turned her Iranian childhood into a universal tale." Other French political and cultural figures also expressed their admiration for her contributions to literature and cinema and her advocacy for women's rights and democracy.

cards.headline: Ted Danson Apologizes for 1993 Blackface Performance at Whoopi Goldberg Roast
cards.teaser: The actor said he will continue apologizing for performing in blackface at a 1993 roast, calling the decision arrogant and stupid.
cards.body:
Ted Danson said he will apologize for the rest of his life for performing in blackface at a 1993 roast of Whoopi Goldberg. Speaking on W. Kamau Bell's podcast Who's With Me?, the Cheers and The Good Place actor discussed the incident, which took place at the New York Friars Club while he and Goldberg were in a relationship.

Danson described the performance as arrogant and stupid. The 1993 roast drew significant criticism at the time and has remained a controversial moment in his career. The actor's comments on the podcast represent his ongoing acknowledgment of the offense caused by the performance.

cards.headline: VFX Giant DNEG Acquires Canary Islands Animation Studio Anima Kitchen
cards.teaser: DNEG's acquisition is backed by a $28.8 million investment from Spain's state-owned venture capital fund.
cards.body:
VFX company DNEG has acquired Canary Islands animation studio Anima Kitchen. The deal is supported by Spain's Society for Technological Transformation, a state-owned sovereign venture capital fund that invested 24.9 million euros, equivalent to $28.8 million, in Anima Kitchen.

The joint investment aims to strengthen the Canary Islands animation studio's capabilities. DNEG is a major player in visual effects production, and the acquisition expands its presence in European animation and production facilities.

cards.headline: Bob Odenkirk Drops Out of Film Project, David Cross to Replace Him
cards.teaser: Odenkirk will not appear in Freedom 250, but his longtime comedy partner David Cross will take his place in the project.
cards.body:
Bob Odenkirk has withdrawn from the film Freedom 250, and David Cross will replace him. The announcement comes after the comedians appeared together in Bob and David Climb Machu Picchu, a film at this year's Tribeca Festival. Directed by Michael LaHaie, that documentary follows the two longtime friends and Mr. Show collaborators on a trek to Machu Picchu.

Cross and Odenkirk have worked together for decades, dating back to their cult comedy series Mr. Show. The substitution keeps Cross involved in Freedom 250 while allowing Odenkirk to step away from the project.

cards.headline: Cannes Festival Director Reflects on Hollywood Restructuring and Competition Lineup
cards.teaser: Thierry Fremaux addressed the 79th Cannes Film Festival's Hollywood presence and competition films after this year's event concluded.
cards.body:
Thierry Fremaux, director of the Cannes Film Festival, reflected on the 79th edition of the event, which wrapped recently. The festival faced familiar criticism about fewer Hollywood blockbusters and American stars, along with a competition lineup that delivered well-received films but no immediate consensus masterpiece.

Fremaux disagreed with the negative assessments, saying he sees Cannes as more competitive, influential, and vital than ever.

cards.headline: France Prepares Bayeux Tapestry for Transport to London
cards.teaser: French officials say the 950-year-old work will be kept as safe as a baby during its upcoming move to London.
cards.body:
The Bayeux Tapestry, an 11th-century embroidery depicting the Norman Conquest of England, is being transported to London in a carefully planned operation across the Channel. French Minister of Culture Catherine Pégard emphasized that nothing has been left to chance in the preparation process.

The tapestry will be placed in a specially constructed cradle within a protective container to ensure it experiences no jolts, bumps, shakes, or vibrations during the journey. This historic loan marks a significant moment for the ancient artifact, which is considered one of the most important medieval works in existence.

cards.headline: Universal Music Greater China Signs Jason Zhang in Multi-Faceted Deal
cards.teaser: The record label signed one of Chinese-language pop's most commercially successful artists to a deal covering recording, management

hero.headline: Senate begins debate on reconciliation package to fund immigration enforcement
hero.teaser: The Senate started debate Thursday on a budget reconciliation package that would fund immigration enforcement agencies through the end of President Trump's term.
hero.body:
The Senate launched debate Thursday on a budget reconciliation package to fund immigration enforcement agencies through the end of Trump's term. After a party-line procedural vote Wednesday, lawmakers prepared for hours of debate followed by a vote-a-rama—a series of rapid-fire amendment votes.

The reconciliation process allows passage with a simple majority, letting Republicans advance the immigration enforcement funding without Democratic support. The vote-a-rama permits senators to propose unlimited amendments voted on in succession, sometimes stretching for hours. Final passage is expected later this week, after which the legislation must be reconciled with any House version before reaching the president.

cards.headline: Deb Haaland wins New Mexico Democratic primary for governor
cards.teaser: The former Biden administration official could become the first female Native American governor if elected in November.
cards.body:
Former Biden administration official Deb Haaland won the Democratic primary for New Mexico governor. If elected in the general election, she would become the first female Native American to serve as a state governor.

Haaland's primary victory secures the Democratic nomination in a state where the party has held the governorship since 2011. The general election will determine whether she achieves this historic milestone.

cards.headline: California governor primary results show Hilton, Becerra leading
cards.teaser: Early returns in the California gubernatorial primary show Republican Steve Hilton and Democrat Xavier Becerra ahead as the race to replace Gavin Newsom takes shape.
cards.body:
Republican Steve Hilton and Democrat Xavier Becerra are narrowly leading California's gubernatorial primary as vote-counting continues. State election officials are working through uncounted ballots in a process that could take days or weeks to complete.

Under California's top-two primary system, the two highest vote-getters regardless of party will advance to the November general election. Becerra, a former U.S. health and human services secretary, is followed by billionaire Democrat Tom Steyer in the race to replace Governor Gavin Newsom.

cards.headline: Democrats eye New Jersey House seat amid Republican incumbent's absence
cards.teaser: Party officials see an opportunity to flip a toss-up district as Rep. Thomas Kean Jr. has been largely absent from Washington.
cards.body:
Democrats view Rep. Thomas Kean Jr.'s New Jersey district as a prime pickup opportunity following his extended absences from Washington. Kean secured the Republican nomination Tuesday for another term representing the west-central part of the state.

The seat is considered a toss-up in a competitive region. Democrats believe Kean's time away from the Capitol provides ammunition for their campaign and positions the district as vulnerable in the upcoming election. Party strategists see it as a critical target for expanding their House majority.

cards.headline: Spencer Pratt advances in Los Angeles mayoral race
cards.teaser: The former reality TV star is close to securing a spot in the runoff election for mayor of Los Angeles.
cards.body:
Spencer Pratt, known for his appearances on reality television, is nearing a position in the Los Angeles mayoral runoff. His performance in the primary election has raised questions about his prospects in a final two-candidate race for leadership of the nation's second-largest city.

Pratt's political trajectory represents an unconventional path to municipal office. His presence in the race has drawn attention to the evolving nature of candidate profiles in major urban elections, though his ability to compete in a runoff against a more traditional political opponent remains uncertain.

cards.headline: New World screwworm confirmed in Texas for first time in 60 years
cards.teaser: The deadly cattle pest was found in Zavala County, prompting an emergency response from the Agriculture Department.
cards.body:
The U.S. Department of Agriculture confirmed a case of New World screwworm in Zavala County, Texas, late Wednesday, marking the first appearance of the pest in the United States since its effective eradication six decades ago. The larvae, which burrow into cattle, have prompted an emergency response from federal agricultural officials.

The discovery comes as the U.S. beef herd has shrunk to its smallest size in 75 years, with retail beef prices at record highs. The screwworm had been feared by the cattle industry since recent outbreaks elsewhere, and the confirmation in Texas raises concerns about potential impacts on an already strained livestock sector.

cards.headline: Senate Democrats weigh Iowa, Maine prospects in fight for chamber control
